utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-03-69-T. The Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. There are a few procedural matters which I'd like to go through in the next couple of minutes. First of all, the Chamber received information that Mr. Knoops is, for reasons he explained to the Chamber, is not able to attend court, and, therefore, Mr. Jordash is representing Mr. Stanisic. I further would like to put on the record that earlier we have discussed the possible housekeeping session on Friday. Unless we find sufficient time today and tomorrow to deal with housekeeping matters which would require approximately five quarters of an hour, perhaps even one hour, any -- it would surprise me if we would go beyond one and a half hours. But if we do find time today or tomorrow, hereby a housekeeping session is scheduled for Friday morning at 9.00. Next, on this housekeeping session, the parties will be informed about the decision of the Chamber that new pseudonyms should be used even for witnesses which have testified in other cases. Therefore, it's of no use to wait giving this decision effect until it has been officially pronounced. Therefore, the Prosecution is invited to review it. The pseudonym -- the pseudonyms that were assigned to witnesses who will testify before Friday. Then the last matter is -- first of all, I'd like to put on the record the following: On the 15th of February of this year, the Chamber was informed via an e-mail from the Stanisic Defence co-counsel to the Chamber's Legal Officer, which was copied to the Prosecution and the Simatovic Defence, that the Stanisic Defence did not oppose the Simatovic Defence urgent Defence request for adjournment filed on the 11th of February of 2010. This is now officially put on the record. Finally, Mr. Bakrac has asked an opportunity to briefly reply to the response to this same motion the Prosecution has filed. Mr. Bakrac, you have five minutes to briefly reply to the Prosecution response. And the Prosecution will be given an opportunity to have the last submission. Mr. Bakrac, I'm looking at the clock, five minutes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you very much for allowing me this opportunity to reply. First of all, I would like to say that the OTP, in their response to our motion, say that we did not find room for the assistance provided to us by the OTP. I would like to say that we are grateful to the OTP for having disclosed 60.000 disclosed documents on two hard disks. They tried to compress everything in one place. However, the OTP is not in a position to read on behalf the Defence, to analyse on behalf of the Defence, and to assist the Defence to come up with a strategy based on the analysis of documents. I'm very grateful to the OTP. I know they are always ready to assist, but what they cannot do is to read on our behalf, to analyse the documents on our behalf, and come up with a strategy of our Defence, and, thus, call the key witnesses. We had two linkage witnesses among the crime based witnesses, and you can see that we used only those documents that Mr. Petrovic and I obtained since we have been appointed. I -- it is not my intention to criticise the former Defence team because I'm still pained by the tragic death of my late colleague, however, I have to say that we did not find anything that the former Defence had done. And we enter the court, we're two and a half months into the trial, we are grateful to the Trial Chamber for having shown understanding both for that and for giving us the gracious period of a month. However, when we look at the things realistically with an intention to provide our client with a professional assistance and to provide him with the right to a fair trial, we have realised that since the 1st of March when you granted for the linkage witnesses to be heard without any exceptions, we cannot follow that rate if we are not granted another break, another recess, to focus our efforts on the linkage witnesses in co-operation with our client who is certainly going to assist us with that. These are the reasons why we did not submit our request earlier. We submitted it only when we realised where we were, when we took stock of the situation. We started with Slobodan Lazarevic in a true -- too broad a manner. We did not manage to examine him in the foreseen time. With all due respect to all the problems of the Tribunal, you have to appreciate our effort to carry out our job professionally and to protect the interests of our client and his right to a fair trial. I don't want to waste much more time on that. I have two more minutes left. Both -- all the parties to these proceedings have been preparing for six years. My colleague Petrovic and I were preparing only for two and a half months. We entered into the courtroom; we are not complaining; we are just looking at things realistically, and we believe that in the upcoming period when we will be facing a linkage witnesses, we will need a six-week break in order to be well prepared for all the upcoming witnesses. The OTP's calculation is 513 days, that have already been spent in these proceedings, but there are reasons for that. The first was the illness of one of the clients and then the tragic death of our colleague, so none of those were due to the -- any of the shortcomings of the Defence, which was given a minimum time to prepare. So what was spent so far is not -- was not at the expense of this Defence team. I believe that I have used my five minutes. This is as much as I wanted to say about the Prosecution's response. And, once again, I would like to thank the OTP. The OTP has provided its opinion. They could have stated that the Defence team should not be given room to prepare. The OTP has left it up to the Trial Chamber to be the Judge of that. And, just for the record, I would like to thank my learned friend Mr. Groome and his team for having been so co-operative. I believe that the reply that they submitted shows their willingness to co-operate. And, once again, I apologise that in our written response we did not emphasise that strongly enough. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. Mr. Groome, would you like to think about whether or not to respond and/or are you already in a position to immediately respond?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, there's no new information or argument I wish to put before the Chamber. Simply I'll rely on the written submissions that we've made in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Chamber will consider the motion. Mr. Jordash, may I take it that in view of your earlier position that there's no need at this moment to further respond to what Mr. Bakrac has just submitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then the -- is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Can I ask for just a few seconds to reassign a pseudonym, Your Honour, before I call out the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am sorry. The Judges had to discuss some computer problems. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution now calls JF-009, and the examination will be conducted by Mr. Hoffmann. Your Honour, it just occurs to me whether it would be useful to go into private session and draw the connection between the new pseudonym and the old pseudonym so that the record is clear. The Chamber issued orders with respect to the old pseudonym on the 8th of February with respect to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Meanwhile, I put on the record that the Chamber has received the weekly report which, as far as we can see, doesn't change the situation, although there was a matter of suffering pain caused by renal stones I think it was. If that would continue and if that would cause major problems, then, of course, the Chamber would like to be informed about it. But apart from that, I don't think that there are any specific questions to be put in this context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness JF-009, because that's how we are going to call you in this case, before you give testimony, the rules require that you make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Please be seated. Witness JF-009, you will testify under protective measures. That means no one outside the courtroom can see your face, and we will not use your own name. If any of the questions that are put to you would be at risk, when answering them, to reveal your identity, you may address me and ask to go into private session so that you can answer the question without revealing your identity. I'm saying this because your testimony, the content of it, can be heard by the outside world. So if there's any answer you'd like to give which would reveal your identity or reveal such clues, such keys, to your identity, don't hesitate to ask me to go into private session. You will first be examined by Mr. Hoffmann, Mr. Hoffmann is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Hoffmann, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And good afternoon, Witness. The Court already informed you about protective measures, and I would ask the Court Usher to just hand to you a new pseudonym sheet. I know that you have -- had signed one before, but it had a different number so that's why I'm -- simply for that reason, I'm asking you to look at this sheet again and sign it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, the Chamber doesn't see the merits in signing it if the witness says this is what my name is. We know what has been shown to him. Then, if it's uploaded in e-court, then there's no need for signatures anymore. But, of course, this now says "signature," so let's, for the last time, then ask the witness to sign the pseudonym sheet. But it doesn't change anything, a signature yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: No, I just changed the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And, Witness, maybe can you just confirm that at the bottom of the page you see the name of your own village on that piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: It would help if you actually give an answer to the microphone so it's recorded. If you just nod, we can see it but it's not recorded. So I invite you to just say yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you see the name of your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. And we will only refer to your home village and not give the name of that village in order to protect your identity.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And then, Your Honours, I would move this pseudonym sheet into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the witness will sign it. So, Witness, whenever we are talking about your home village, we are talking about that village of which you saw the name. Is that clear to you? And could you please come a bit closer to the microphones. Please proceed, Mr. Hoffmann. Oh yes, and we have to -- Madam Registrar, the pseudonym sheet would receive number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P251 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P251 is admitted under seal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall giving a statement to investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would then ask that we see 65 ter 5229 on the screen, a statement of this witness, ERN 0202-1846 to 0202-1854, an ICTY witness statement dated 13 March 2001. May I ask that it not be broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, on the screen before you, you see a document purporting to be a statement that you gave to the ICTY investigators on the 13th March, 2001. Do you recall giving a statement on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And if we, please, could go to page 8 of the English document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: May I ask you, sir, to look at the signature on this page and ask you whether you recognise your own signature on this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And did you have an opportunity, prior to testifying today, to review this statement in your own language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And did that statement that you signed in 2001 accurately reflect what you said to the Office of the Prosecutor at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And if you were asked the same questions as in 2001, would you, today, give the same answers in substance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution would ask that the prior statement of this witness from 2001 be admitted into evidence. That is 65 ter 5229, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P252 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P252 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement which is now Exhibit P252 - and it is, in English, at page 3, paragraph 3, the same for the B/C/S - you describe how Serb soldiers came to your village in April 1992. Can you tell the Court, first of all, the ethnicity of the people who were living in your village at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: The majority of residence in our village were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness, please repeat what he said after this one. We didn't catch that, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters heard you say that the majority in your village were Muslims. You added something to that, could you repeat the last part of your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was only one Serbian house in our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: You describe the Serb soldiers had camouflage uniforms and black bandanas. On the sleeves they wore the four Serb S. Can you tell the Court if those Serb soldiers were locals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: How would you know that they were not locals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, according to their voices, I noticed that they were not local.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly that you refer to their pronunciation or their dialect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, the accent that they had was not from the local area. They were from abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: If you say they were from abroad, do you know or did you have any idea where from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court if you recall what happened to the mosque in your village?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat. It was inaudible. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat again. May I invite you, again, to come close to the microphone and to clearly repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The mosque was demolished by Predrag Kujundzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And when did that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: I remember only that it was on the second day of Bajram.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Are you still referring to the year 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Further on in your statement - Exhibit P252, and this is at page 4 - you describe your detention at the so-called Percin's Disco. Can you tell the Court who was detained at that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Detained there were Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Did those detainees include men, women, and children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: All the men were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And those men, were those members of any armed forces, or were these civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: They were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: In your statement you describe the soldiers guarding the disco, and you mention that some of them wore red berets. Can you tell the Court if those were members of any specific unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, I think that they belonged to a special unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And what made you believe that they were a special unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, most probably, although I hadn't seen that army before, I heard them talking and I heard their accent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: So this is the reason how you distinguish the Red Berets from other units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, you have mentioned Predrag Kujundzic just a few moments ago. Were you able to distinguish the unit that you call Red Berets from the men of Predrag Kujundzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to object. I don't think the witness did call the unit the Red Berets. I think the Prosecution called the unit the Red Berets. The witness simply said that the group -- that there was some people wearing red berets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may. I didn't want to react initially, but on page 12, my learned friend, in line 25, asked the witness to describe the soldiers who were guarding the disco club, and he cited a portion from his statement, and you said you mentioned Red Berets also. When you look at Exhibit 252, the only place where it's mentioned is page 4, but it's phrased differently. It says there were various soldiers who came, some of them had red berets, some of them had camouflage units. So I think that the witness statement was misinterpreted in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic. If you want to object against an inaccurate quote of the witness's statement, then you shouldn't wait for half a page and then to join Mr. Jordash. It is clear to us, however, that the statement talks about some people wearing camouflage uniforms and some people, or some soldiers I think it even says, wearing red berets. And reference to red berets is understood in the context of this statement. Please rephrase your question as you announced you would do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And just for the record, I think I just quoted literally from the statement saying that some of them wore red berets as it said in the English statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, you had mentioned Predrag Kujundzic and his men. And my question to you is if you could distinguish Predrag Kujundzic's men from those that you saw wearing red berets and that you referred to as a special unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And can you explain to the Chamber how you could tell the two units apart?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: It was quite simple to distinguish them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you explain and expand on that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, Predrag's Army, most of them, were locals, our neighbours. As for the Red Berets, I only recognised them by their accents, because they spoke differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you describe how those that you refer to as the Red Berets, how they were dressed, apart from their red berets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: They also had camouflage uniforms and four Ss. They had kerchiefs and some of them had hats on their heads.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, when did you see the people that you refer to as Red Berets for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: As soon as we arrived at Percin's Disco.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you give the Court maybe an example of any particular day or situation when you saw the Red Berets at the disco?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, on that day during Bajram when we were brought there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Did you see them again after that first day of detention at the disco?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: In what situation or context did that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: They were stationed in a house there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Just for the record, if you say they were stationed in a house there, are you referring to the vicinity of the Percin's Disco?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And how often would you see the Red Berets at the disco?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: What were they doing at the disco when you saw them there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: For the most part they were just strolling around and doing some exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Did you ever see them inside the disco building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement at - and that is at page 4, paragraph 5 - you describe how one day a soldier ordered 50 detainees to come out and how these were subsequently used as human shields. Do you recall the actual date when that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: I know that was St. Peter's Day. It was their patron saint's day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Do you recall the date or the month of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: I think the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Final question: The 12th of which month, if you do remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you describe to the Court the soldier that was taking the detainees out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: One soldier burst inside with a rifle. He had a camouflage uniform on, and he requested 50 men to come outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember if that particular soldier belonged to any specific unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Most probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court to which unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: The Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Further on in your statement - and we're still at page 4, the last paragraph - you describe how you were told to take off your shirts and form a number of rows when moving to the front line. Can you tell the Court what happened next after you took off your shirts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: After we took our shirts off, they ordered us to walk towards Plane. We were in several files.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Do you recall if any of the detainees that was brought there was killed at the beginning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: When we set off, one of them came and shot a man in the head. And he just told us this is what will happen to you if you try to escape.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Are you able to describe the person who shot this detainee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: He was in a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Anything else that you remember apart from the uniform, what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: He also had a red beret on his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Could you tell whether he was a local soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer. It was inaudible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you, again, give the answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I could tell because most of them were strangers, those Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And by strangers, you mean not locals; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: No, no, they were not locals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your question is ambiguous. If you say "you mean not locals," what you intended to say is "you mean non-locals." That creates the confusion. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Do you know that person that was killed, the detainee who was shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: I only heard his name, but I do know that he was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And would you know from what village he was from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Dragalovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell the Court what happened to Safet Hamidovic during that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Safet Hamidovic was killed on the way back, again by the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And what happened to his body then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: We were ordered to throw his body into the River Bosna.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- I noticed that two different names are used. If you look at page 18 and -- page 18 line 1 and compare it -- no, it seemed to be different but apparently it's corrected. There was for a little moment different names, but apparently there was a mistake. I would make far more mistakes if I would have to transcribe these hearings, and, so, therefore, I'm always surprised that only such a little number of mistakes are made. Mr. Hoffmann, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Actually, in front of my screen, you are right; in the answer it still gives a different spelling, so ... it should read Safet Hamidovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the spelling is slightly different still. In view of the statement given by the witness, is there, and I'm also addressing the Defence, would there be any dispute as to whether the person the question was about is the same person as the witness mentioned in his answer? Then we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me, I have nothing to say about this particular person. It is not in dispute. There is something else which is in dispute and that is that the Defence has never been informed about what this witness was going to testify about. We have his statement, P252. It has five or six pages. The Red Berets are mentioned for the first time on page four, line 3. The second source is additional information provided to us by my learned friend on the paragraph -- on the -- February 10th, 2010, where it reads that the witness knew about the existence of the Red Berets, he knew they were not locals, and he knew that only on the basis of his -- of their accent. Now, we are hearing about some very serious allegations made at the expense of the people wearing red berets. This is what we hear for the first time, and we are not ready for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, I -- it's the witness's answer. Of course, Mr. Hoffmann is unable to tell -- we'll have a look at it and if this causes specific problems in preparing for your cross-examination, Mr. Petrovic, we'd like to hear that. And, meanwhile, we'll carefully check how the testimony was elicited from the witness in this respect and compare that with the written statement we have received. Meanwhile, please proceed, Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: If you allow me, just a quick note on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: The statement that was tendered, in fact, refers to Serb soldiers at various times. I think the Defence is well aware that there are a number of prior statements. Again, to be more efficient, we haven't tendered those prior statements, but they make extensive reference to the Red Berets just in the context of the testimony that we just heard now. So I think there is no surprise in what this witness is testifying about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To rely on previous statements which give details with are not found in the statement tendered is -- to say that there's no surprise at all might be a bit of an overstatement. We'll have a fellow look into it. Please proceed for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: If at any time I can be of more assistance, I have reference to each of the statements and where the Red Berets are mentioned in the context. But I'll proceed for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, we are still talking about the 12th of July, 1992, when you were at the front line. And my question to you is if you recall if on that day, at that incident, any of the Serb soldiers or policemen was injured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Do you happen to know his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And do you know what happened to this Serb who got injured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: I only know that that Croat saved him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: What Croat are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, that one who was with us as part of the human shield.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: So just to be clear on the record, he was one of the detainees from the disco, you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And do you happen to know the name of that Croatian detainee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, did you have a chance to review a number of photos from Doboj prior to coming to testify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would ask that we please see Exhibit P87 on the screen. That is formerly 65 ter 5169. And I would ask that we go to page 14 of that collection, which is showing photo number 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, now, looking at this photo number 10 of Exhibit P87, can you tell the Court what building we see on this photo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: You mean the building in the middle?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what this building is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: That used to be the disco once in the past.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Again, just for the record, so this is the Percin's Disco you referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes, that disco, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Today, earlier, you have mentioned that the Red Berets were stationed in the vicinity in a house. Do you see that, by any chance, on this picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would ask that the Court Usher please assist the witness with marking this photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And, sir, I would ask you to indicate with a red X, the place you say the Red Berets were stationed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And would you mind, at the bottom of this photo, to put down your pseudonym, JF-009.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this photo of P87 as marked by the witness be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? No. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P253, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Again, Mr. Hoffmann, the purpose of signing or initialing documents is that if the document comes at a later stage to the Court, that by putting that signature or those initials on that document, that we have a means of verification that that's the same document the witness said something about in his statement or whatever, and it's not another document. Now, both in respect of pseudonym sheets, but also in respect of photographs, the Chamber doesn't need to verify that because the Chamber has seen it. Therefore, the whole purpose of initials and/or signatures on documents which were presented in front of the Chamber and to which the witness testified is -- doesn't serve any purpose, as far as I can see. But if you have any purpose in mind, then please tell us what that would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I think the additional purpose is to have, at a later stage, a reference even if that document would ever be coming up in another trial, whatever, that you immediately have a reference to who did that marking. If you would have just a red cross on it, without the transcript, it wouldn't be clear. But we are happy to follow your instructions on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree, I was mainly thinking about what purpose it would serve for this trial. So, therefore, we agree on that. And if you think that it's likely to be used in any other trial and for that purpose you would like to have it initialled, then I'm not going to spend any further words on it. I think it has been admitted into evidence. Yes, and just for the record, apart from the cross, we find a few lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether it has been stored already, but I know that --

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I'm being told these three additional lines which happened by mistake can be taken off before we save it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, before we save it, we take out the three lines which, by mistake, were made. Yes, that's one, that's two. Thank you, Madam Usher. Then the document is admitted, is now without the three additional lines. Only the initials of the witness and the cross at the house in the background. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we then please go back to Exhibit P87 to page 47. Page 47 showing photo number 43 of that collection.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, if you just take a look at it and then I'll ask that we see the next photo on page 48 as well. Sir, looking at those two pictures, do you recognise the buildings that are depicted on these photos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court what buildings these are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: These are hangars. And the buildings used to be a warehouse near Bosanka Doboj, that's the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And are those the hangars that you describe in your statement as being detained there for a few days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would then ask that we call up Prosecution 65 ter Exhibit 5232. It's ERN 0674-2885.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, did you, prior to testifying today, review this list of names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And in the first column, did you mark any person that you remember by name as being detained with you at the Percin's Disco?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And in the very last column, did you mark any detainee that you remember being killed on 12 July 1992 while being used as human shields?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution tenders this document, this list of victims of the 12th of July, 1992, into evidence. As it has the previous pseudonym for the time being, I would ask that we admit it under seal. And maybe we can redact the old pseudonym which is at the bottom of the page with his signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P254 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P254 is admitted under seal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm just looking at the clock, I may have about slightly over five minutes left, therefore, I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that we would continue. Usually we take sessions of 75 minutes. It would be a little bit over 75 minutes. Please proceed, Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Sir, when you were released from detention in late summer 1992 and you refer to that in your statement at page 6, paragraph 3, what did you do after being released from the detention?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: I was subject to work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: At some time were you allowed to return to your own village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And can you describe the situation in the village when you returned in late summer 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: When I returned, I realised that everything had been looted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And finally, in your 2001 statement - Exhibit P252 at page 6, last paragraph - you describe how, in July of 1993, all villagers were transported out of Doboj. Can you tell the Court if you and the other villagers left on your own free will?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Why do you say that you did not leave on your own free will? Can you explain that to the Court, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, because buses arrived to take us, and we had to pay 50 German marks each for transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Did you have a choice to stay behind in your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: No, we had no choice at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what ethnicity the villagers were on the 12 buses that you mention in your 2001 statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Did the group of villagers that you described on the buses include man, women, and children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And were these people on the buses prior to boarding the buses involved in any fighting, or were these civilians, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: They were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And where did the buses bring you to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: All the way to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Did you personally ever return to live in your home village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: I did not have an opportunity to return before. Nobody dared return before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: If you say "returned before," what time-period do you refer to, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, we all spent ten years or even longer living as refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And as of today, did you ever return back to live in your home village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: When did you go back to live in your home village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: I stayed living in the centre of town even a bit longer because I did not have a place to return to since my house had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And when about was that? Which year, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, if my learned friend wants to lead on this, there's no dispute from the Stanisic Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And since there's no strong opposition from the Simatovic Defence, Mr. Hoffmann, if you want to lead, there's no problem in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would just ask you, Witness, did you return in the recent years to your home village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: That being two or three years ago, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Even more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Okay. I'll put it the other way around. It was after 1995, after the war ended; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we take a break, I'd like to seek clarification on one issue. You said you had no choice then to leave because you had to pay 50 Deutschmarks, and you had to board the buses. Who told you that you had to board those buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Red Cross arrived from Doboj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the Red Cross is not known for forcing people out of their homes. What was told to you under those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were told to collect the bare necessities, as the buses were on their way. The police were there. They had arrived together with the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And was that local Red Cross, or was that International Red Cross? Did they speak your language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did not engage in any conversations with them. They just came as escorts to take us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you not hear them speak at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You do not know whether these were foreigners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did they tell you that you had to board the buses, or were they just there and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were there to come with us as our escorts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But, now, who told you exactly that you had to go on those buses? Was it the Red Cross, was it the police, was it anyone else? You said you were informed that you have to take your necessary belongings; who told you that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The police and the Red Cross, but I myself did not understand what they were saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because you didn't know the language, or?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the police that came, what did they speak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do I understand you well that the police came together with the Red Cross and that you could understand the police because they were speaking your language, and that the Red Cross people were not speaking your language? Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was there anyone, as far as you know, who resisted, that is, refused to board the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nobody would have remained there alive. Even if you had been insane, you would not have stayed there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. We first have a break, and we will resume at ten minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Will it be the Stanisic Defence or Simatovic Defence who will cross-examine the witness first?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The Stanisic Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness JF-009, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Jordash. Mr. Jordash is counsel for Mr. Stanisic. Mr. Jordash, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I say, from the outset, that we do not seek to challenge the horrible experience that you had, and we express our sympathy for that experience. I would like, however, to ask you some questions to try to clarify some of the things that you saw during that experience and some of the conclusions that you reached. You follow me? You understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll be about 20 to 30 minutes. Now, you said in response to my learn friend for the Prosecution that you saw men who you now term Red Berets and you recognised them because they had, I think, foreign accents, and you also described them as wearing camouflage uniforms with four Ss on them. And then you said they had kerchiefs and some of them had hats on their heads. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Jordash kindly speak into the microphone, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So the men you term as Red Berets, some of them had hats on their heads and some of them did not; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The men who you term Red Berets who did not have hats on their heads, were they dressed in camouflage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes, they were, but they seemed to be local.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. So some of the men who you term Red Berets who did not have hats on seemed to be local; do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Some of the men who had hats on who you termed Red Berets, were they, some of them, also local?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So the men who you term Red Berets with hats on, were they all, from what you observed, from out of the immediate Doboj region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Most of them were from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Most of the men who wore red berets who term Red Berets were from Serbia; where were the others from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Where were the others from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, they were local, from the area around Ozren and the Doboj area, the entire Doboj area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, you have men wearing red berets, most of them from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And men you also term Red Berets who were from around the Ozren and the Doboj area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I want to be clear about one more thing. The men you term Red Berets who were from around the Ozren and the Doboj area, how did you know that they were -- or why did you see them as Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, they had different insignia. Some had the four Ss, and these others had eagles on their patches. And also, they spoke a different -- they had a different accent.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: A different accent from where? A different accent to which accent? What are you making the comparison to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, they kept using the word "bre."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: B-r-e.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. So the men who had eagles on their patches and spoke with a different accent, did you you know where the accent was from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Where was that from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, they were there outside the disco building.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, let me try that question again. The men who wore eagles on their patches and spoke with a different accent, did you recognise where the accent came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you had men wearing red berets who were from Serbia and men also wearing eagles on their patches who sounded as if they were coming from Serbia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: No, I said that the men who had the eagles on the patches, they were Serbian, and they had -- they kept using the word "bre;" whereas the others were local, they were normal speaking people.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. So let me try to be clear. The men with the eagles on their patches, did you define them to yourself as Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: They were all Red Berets but, as I've already mentioned, the ones who also had the eagles, they were from Serbia; whereas the guys who had the four Ss, they were local.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, it's probably my lack of understanding, but could you then define for us who you say was a Red Beret? How are you defining that specifically? Was it because of the accent or something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, they kept using "bre" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Which is a Serbian localism.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and they had a different accent, a special accent.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So is this, then, and accurate description of your perception: If you heard a soldier at that time using the term "bre," the Serbian localism, you would define them as a Red Beret? Is that -- am I right about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And if they were local, if the soldiers you saw were local with local accent, you would define them as something other than a Red Beret?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, you are confusing the witness here of your -- his previous testimony. The only way of dealing with the matter is to go through in a very systematic way, step by step. Let me see whether I can give it a start. There were persons you called Red Berets. You've told us that you've seen persons wearing Red Berets. Now, was every person wearing a red beret, are they among what you call the Red Berets? If you would see someone with a red beret, would you automatically say that is a Red Beret?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, if someone was not wearing a red beret but was wearing the kind of hat you described, would you call those Red Berets, would you always call those persons Red Berets, or would you need additional information to call them Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they all had these red caps, red berets. But they had different insignia. Some had eagles, and the others had four Ss.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you. We'll come to the insignia at a later stage. You told us there were people wearing red berets, and you also told us people were wearing hats. Now, if someone would wear a hat, as you described it, would that mean for you that that was a Red Beret, in itself, just by looking at the hat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you could wear a hat without being a Red Beret, for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Possibly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, people not wearing any head cover at all, did you see them just without berets, without hats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there were troops and military personnel of all sorts. You couldn't even tell all the different uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But were there soldiers not wearing red berets, not wearing the hats as you described them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would -- among those, would there be any who, although not wearing a red beret, although not wearing a hat, you would, nevertheless, consider to be among what you called the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, my next question is: If you say people were wearing red berets, you saw people wearing hats, are you aware of persons wearing a red beret, well, let's say, in the morning and wearing a hat in the afternoon? Did they change their hat wear at any time? If you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there were such instances. There were people without any hats on. There were also -- there were also bald people -- bald people, and there were all kinds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's just take, for an example, the bald people. They were automatically not Red Berets for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were, in fact, true Red Berets because I saw these men every day, they practice in the use of arms and also all different types of martial arts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say, by what you saw as training exercises, you would say that even not wearing a red beret or not wearing a hat they, nevertheless, could be among those you considered to be Red Berets; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I move to a different aspect, insignia. Were there insignia that were worn only by persons you would call Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there were -- there was also -- there were military personnel who just had regular insignia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But now, could you give me an example of what you consider a specific Red Beret insignia, if that exists? If you know. If you don't know, tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They only had the eagle patches, eagles insignia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand you well, you earlier mentioned the eagles insignia, that if someone was wearing an eagle insignia, if he was wearing eagle insignia, you considered that person to be a Red Beret. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and that they were from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll come to the language at a later stage. Did you ever see anyone wearing eagle insignia which you would say were, nevertheless, not Red Berets, or?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that's not possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By wearing the eagle insignia, they fell within the category of Red Berets for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, those wearing eagle insignia, were they always also wearing red berets, or could you wear eagle insignia without wearing a red beret as head cover?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's possible because there were times when they took their caps off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would the same be true for the hats, that is, that you could -- well, I think that question is answered already by the previous question. Any other insignia you considered to be indicative, being an indication that someone would be part of, you call, altogether, the Red Berets? Do you recall any of the other insignia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Earlier, the four Ss insignia were mentioned. Have you seen those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, same question as with the eagle insignia: If you would wear a four Ss insignia, would that mean automatically that you are a Red Beret, or could it be that you are not a Red Beret, nevertheless, wearing the four Ss insignia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if you were wearing four Ss insignia, you were a Red Beret; and, similarly, if you were wearing an eagle insignia you would be a Red Beret as well, in your understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Irrespective of whether you really were wearing, at that moment, a hat or a red beret, it's the insignia that were significant for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did I understand you well that if you were wearing those insignia, it could well be that you would have a red beret as head cover or such a hat as you described as head cover, so that means insignia and such head cover?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you told us that some people were using specific language which you recognised as specifically Serb. Now -- we have, now, the Red Berets that are people with those insignia whether or not wearing the red berets or the hats; would all of those, wearing these insignia, would all of those speak the specific Serb language, or would there be, among them, soldiers who would speak your local dialect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Earlier, you told us that Red Berets often were using this Serb language but that there were local Red Berets as well. Now, could you explain to me what you then considered to be local Red Berets? What insignia were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They wore the four Ss; that insignia. Locals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I earlier asked you, I said, Were all of those wearing these insignia - and I was referring to the four Ss insignia and eagle insignia - I asked you would they all speak the specific Serb language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or would, among them, there also be soldiers who would speak your local language. And then you said, "No," at the time. Now your answer is different. You say those wearing the -- you said that some of the locals were - and you recognised them by their language I do understand -- that nevertheless some of the locals were also wearing the four Ss insignia. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And as far as the eagles insignia are concerned, were there any people speaking your local language which would wear the eagles insignia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I only mentioned that for the people from Serbia. But there were also locals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say "there were also locals," wearing the eagle insignia, or?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the four Ss; that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what I now understand from you is then that those wearing eagle insignia were always speaking the specific Serb language, whereas --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- those wearing the four Ss insignia, that they could either speak the Serb specific language or your local dialect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our local dialect and Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would find, among those, people speaking specific Serbian but also persons speaking your own language. I said I would give it a start, Mr. Jordash. I may have disappointed you. I went on quite a bit. Not to say that we've exhausted the subject, but a very systematic approach. I thought, that would assist the Chamber, at least. Not to say that it would resolve all problems, but at least it would assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. And, as I said before, don't consider the matter to be exhausted, if you have any specific further questions on the matter, which -- but preferably aiming at seeking clarification rather than further confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Certainly. I think I hope to do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, have you seen, since 1992, the eagle insignia that you speak of? Have you been shown it by the Prosecution? Have you been shown a book with insignia in it and asked to identify it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: No one has to show me. I know what an eagle is and what four Ss are, so I don't need to be shown anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You haven't been shown it by the Prosecution in the last few days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: There's no need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ... You've told us now two times that there's no need to do a certain thing. What I'd like to know is that, with or without any need, whether you were shown a book or pictures of insignia, or whether they were never shown to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did the description you've just given at the learned Judge concerning the Ss and the insignia, did you give that to the Prosecution a few days ago when Mr. Hoffmann interviewed you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes, I told him about the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the account you gave before the break concerning the Red Berets being part of the human shield, training outside of where you were detained, was that an account you gave to Mr. Hoffmann a few days ago when he interviewed you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And was he taking notes when you gave him that account? Was he writing or typing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, I did observe that he did write something down, but what it was, I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You met Mr. Hoffmann on the 15th of February, 2010. 15th of February, a few days ago, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And how long were you interviewed for during that appointment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, up until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What time did you start; do you remember, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And during that two hours, was Mr. Hoffmann writing notes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to ask you about Predrag Kujundzic. Just a few questions about him. He came to your village in June of 1992. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And he was born on Mount Ozren; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And he had a paramilitary or a military unit called Preda's Wolves; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Preda's, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And did they are the men who surrounded your village so that you couldn't get out; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And did they have any insignias, those men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: The four Ss. And they wore camouflage uniforms and black kerchiefs.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But no eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the men who you saw surrounding your town, did you see them taking orders from Predrag?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Predrag actually sent the troops into the village, and he issued orders to people as to what they were to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And was Predrag -- sorry, let me start that again. Did Predrag have the four Ss on his uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But no eagle on his uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: That's correct; no eagles.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And his brother, you saw his brother being part of that group surrounding your village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And his brother was called Nenad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And his --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. And his brother also had four Ss on his uniform but no eagle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Four Ss.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And no eagle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And were all these men, as far as you could hear, local men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Local men.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And these local men had lists and were looking specifically for local people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, the men who gathered you at Percin's Disco were regular policemen wearing blue uniforms; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And those policemen, at different occasions, allowed various soldiers to come in and mistreat you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And it's right that the men you said were Red Berets didn't come inside the disco; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, I said that a soldier entered, a soldier wearing a camouflage uniform. Whether he had a Red Beret on, I didn't really notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The men coming into mistreat and beat you were local people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes, local people.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The man you saw -- am I correct that you saw the man, the soldier, kill the Croat man? Did you see that with your own eyes? The Croat man from Dragalovci.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Are you able to describe the man who shot that Croat man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: He was wearing a camouflage uniform, and he shot him from a very close range. He shot him in the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know where the man was from, the man who did the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you hear him speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Didn't you hear him warn the rest of you in the shield that if anyone tried to escape or didn't do what they were told, they would suffer the same consequence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you hear his accent? Where was it from? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, most probably he was a local man, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was the man who did the shooting -- let me start that again. Did the man who shot the Croat man take orders from someone at the scene, from another soldier at the scene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was the man who shot the Croat man, did he appear to be in charge, or was he one of the criminals pushing you into the human shield?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: I didn't hear your question. I wasn't following quite.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'll repeat it. The man who shot the Croat man, did he appear to be in command or was he just one of the criminals pushing you into the human shield?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, he just barged inside, and he asked for 50 men to be taken outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And that's the same man who shot the Croat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now -- one moment, please. Do you know a man called Karaga; is that correct? Or you met a man called Karaga when you were detained? Sorry, Let me repeat that: Do you recall a man called Karaga?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: He was a local man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you observe him with his group when you were detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes. He also was one of those who entered the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was he then taking orders from Predrag?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: I wouldn't know about that. He had his own soldiers, and I don't know whom he received his orders from.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm not disputing that he had his own soldiers, but why did you come to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, he had his men. He came all the time while I was in detention, and I also knew him from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the man who was in his group were also local men, from what you can see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And did they have any insignias, Karaga's group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What did they have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: They had four Ss.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And that was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: That was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did they have anything on their heads?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Well, for the most part, they wore hats.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you see the colour? Do you recall the colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-009
utterances.text: Camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I please have on the screen Exhibit 253.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I just want to understand, if I can. Do you have that on your screen, Mr. Witness? The house that you have drawn the red cross on, who do you say lived there?
